summary: Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. In 1890, he studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Wilhelm Geiger.

Donald A. Ringe is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bard College, the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Oxford, and Yale University. Around 1985, he joined the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania.

Donald Capps worked in religious studies, having studied at Lewis & Clark College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held posts at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte (~1974-1981) and Princeton Theological Seminary (~1981-2015).

Donald E. Gjertson worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1969-1975) under John Ching-yu Wang, Albert E. Dien, William A. Lyell, and James J. Y. Liu, and later taught at UMass Amherst (~1976-2011).
Donald Harper works in Sinology and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Arizona from around 1990 to 2000 and at the University of Chicago around 2000.

Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Nyanaponika Thera. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970-2004) and Harvard University's Center for the Study of World Religions (2004-2010).
Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who studied at Washington University in St. Louis from around 1960 to 1964. He took up a post at Emory University around 1982.

Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Patrick Olivelle, and Ludo Rocher. He served as an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 2003 to 2014.

Donald S. Lopez Jr., a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (~1974-1982) under Jeffrey Hopkins. His posts include Middlebury College (~1979-1989), the University of Michigan (1990), and the University of Bristol (1997).
Dor Bahadur Bista worked in Tibetology and other fields, having studied at Tri Chandra College. He served as a professor at Tribhuvan University from around 1978 to 1990.
Doranne Jacobson is an Indologist who completed a doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University (~1963-1974). She served as a seminar associate at Columbia University's Southern Asian Institute.
Doris Unterthurner specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Mark Webber and completed an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes around 2017.

Dorji Wangchuk works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed graduate degrees at the University of Hamburg (~1992-2002) under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, becoming a professor there around 2009 after succeeding Jackson.

Dorothy C. Wong specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She joined the faculty at the University of Virginia around 1997 and served as a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong around 2011.

Douglas Matthew Gildow specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Princeton University (~2009-2016) under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou, alongside committee members Jonathan C. Gold, Jacqueline I. Stone, and Robert Wuthnow.

Douglas Ober works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington (~2007-2009) and completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia (~2010-2016) under doctoral supervisor Harjot Oberoi.

Douglas Osto, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, earned a master's at the University of Washington and a PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel (~2001-2004). In 2005, he took up a post at Massey University.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at James Madison University and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, and held posts at Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University (~2007-2014).
Dragana Majhen specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree at the University of Manitoba (~2008-2010), where her thesis advisor was Albert Welter.

Dragomir Dimitrov works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA at the University of Marburg (~1996-2004) under Michael Hahn, held a post there around 2004, and worked on the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.
